discard_or_defer: old release-readiness review coupling is deferred; the new kernel should first enforce boundary resolution
old command-specific shell branch inspection is not copied wholesale; new commands should expose one shared boundary resolver

guarantees.text: Workspace-oriented CLI commands must not default to $REDCAP_ROOT/.dev-task.md.
The default workspace must be the caller's discovered project workspace unless --workspace or REDCAP_WORKSPACE is provided.
The default task file must be <workspace>/.dev-task.md unless --task-file or a backward-compatible positional task file is provided.
When the caller is inside the RedCap runtime repository, the default workspace may equal the runtime root to preserve self-development.
Status and diagnose output must expose runtime root, workspace root, task file, and user-state policy.
Revive must reuse the same workspace/task-file resolution and must not fall back to the RedCap runtime task card when an external workspace has its own task card.
Summary must reuse the same workspace/task-file resolution so human-facing task overviews describe the managed project, not the runtime repository.
Doctor and debug must reuse the same workspace/task-file resolution and must not fall back to the RedCap runtime task card when an external workspace has its own task card.
RedCap self-development remains supported because running the CLI from the RedCap repository makes workspace root equal runtime root.

project.meaning: The project being managed by RedCap, including its task file and project-local workflow state.
project.workspace_discovery: If cwd is inside the RedCap runtime root, default to the runtime root for self-development; otherwise walk upward from cwd for .dev-task.md, falling back to cwd when no task file is found.

runtime.meaning: RedCap's shipped tools, scripts, policies, package metadata, and runtime implementation.

user.meaning: Local user and Agent identity, notification profile, and host-specific state that must not be packed as project state.

portable_rules_for_new_redcap: workspace-oriented commands must resolve project_workspace from caller context, not from RedCap runtime root
task_file defaults to <project_workspace>/.dev-task.md unless explicit task file is supplied
self-development is the only case where project_workspace may equal runtime_root
status/diagnose/debug-style outputs must expose runtime_root, project_workspace, task_file, and user_private_root
user identity and private local state stay outside runtime_root and project_workspace
external project evidence and runtime state must not default into RedCap runtime_root or the managed project workspace
